To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sustained c‐Fos/c‐Jun activities mediate MAP kinase signaling and are essential to differentiation of PC12.
the sustained AP‐1 activities are required for differentiation of PC‐12 cells and that c‐Fos cooperates with Jun proteins to promote differentiation.
sustained ERK, JUN and FOS activities mediate differentiation, while JNK and p38 activities are involved in stress response and apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cell differentiation, cell death and cell growth control.
the mechanisms that underlie the regulation of the transcription factor AP-1 in response to growth and stress signals.
the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal differentiation, and the role of AP‐1 and MAP kinases in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c‐Fos, but not Fra‐2 is required for NGF‐inducible differentiation of PC12 cell.
the sustained c‐Jun/c‐Fos activation by ERK and JNK signaling is a key event in the differentiation of PC12 cell.
c‐Fos expression is not required for differentiation, whereas c‐Jun is essential for differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sustained activation of c‐FOS and c‐JUN proteins is required for neuronal cell differentiation and that this activation is mediated via the JNK and ERKS pathways.
c‐Jun and Fra‐1 are essential for the growth response of PC12 cells, whereas c‐Fos mediates differentiation.
sustained activation of c‐FOS and c‐JUN is required for neuronal PC12 cell differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sustained c‐Fos/Jun activation is essential for differentiation of neuronal cells, but not for growth or apoptosis.
sustained c‐Fos expression and c‐Jun activation are necessary for differentiation of PC 12 cells.
c‐Jun and Fra‐2 play distinct roles in PC12 cell apoptosis and differentiation.
